Every ceiling below is either a measurement of THIS project or a deliberately-kept target with its status recorded. PROJECT_LEARNINGS.md (2,888,991 B at calibration) deliberately gets NO entry: it is on-demand and grep/section-accessed, so per the seed's own rule its budget would sit on the wrong unit (the whole file) — any honest whole-file ceiling is either red forever or records 2.9 MB as the standard. Re-derive with: python3 context_budget.py --calibrate — but see _bytes_per_token before trusting the fit.
_read_cap_tokens: Harness fact, not a policy: the Claude Code whole-file read cap. Matches the 25,000-token constant methodology_dashboard.py v2.18.0 uses for the same purpose (it converts this to a 56,750 B one-read budget for this repo's content).
_bytes_per_token: The densest content measured in THIS repo, as measured by methodology_dashboard.py v2.18.0 (25,000 tok = 56,750 B). Adopted in place of the seed's 2.93 because a local measurement beats an inherited one. S720 ran --calibrate (n=119 sessions, R^2=0.73): it fit 0.60 B/token with a NEGATIVE fixed floor (-6,015 tok) — physically implausible, a confounded regression (opening context here varies with tools/MCP servers loaded, not only CLAUDE.md size) — so the fit was REJECTED, not adopted. Using the densest measured value is the conservative choice: it makes token estimates err high.
_fixed_harness_tokens: Seed value, NOT locally derived — S720's calibration intercept was negative (see _bytes_per_token), so this project has no defensible local measurement. Kept only as framing for the resident-class ceiling; nothing gates on it.
_growth_run: Seed value kept as-is: the trigger that survives ceiling-raising. History lives in .context-budget-history.jsonl, which this project GITIGNORES (S719 decision, matching dashboard_history.jsonl) — so the run resets on a fresh clone. Accepted: this clone is the working one, and the ceilings below are the durable record.
